spiritual_reading:
# Translation into the Spiritual Sense

** ¶7:** For the spiritual life within a person is in this condition . When fals ities and evils take hold of the outer faculties of the mind, and the will grows sluggish toward good, and the interior life is in anguish, and there is suffering throughout from the domin ion of falsity — the person seeks divine wisdom to restore what has been di sordered, to strengthen the will so that it may again receive good. And divine wisdom removes the falsities that have risen up against the inner life , and rest ores the mind to spiritual health. This is what is meant.

**¶8:** And one who possesses ordered divine truths comes , knowing the sequence of tru ths proper to genuine spiritual restoration . When such a one undert akes the regener ation of the person who is spiritu ally sick , he applies the tru ths he knows in their right order — and he even p resses down with the power of the lowest natural truth upon every external faculty of the mind. The person under going regener ation perce ives that this discipline is being applied so that spiritual healing may be accomplished — that it is not done from any opposition or host ility. Rather , everything that divine truth does to the natural mind , it does for the sake of rest oring whol eness to the external man. It expels fals ity and the suffering that comes from evil , pressing hard upon the outer faculties solely to bring about this good . The person being regener ated therefore harb ors no reactive evil nor resent ment against the wisdom that disciplines him. He cannot turn against it in opposition , because he perce ives that all of this is done for his spiritual benefit.

**¶9:** But should evil itself come and assault the fac ulties of the mind out of host ility — the person may resist it , refuse it, and not permit its entrance. For he perce ives that this assault comes from opposition to his spiritual life ; and as evil strikes from its own di sordered desire , it adds further fals ity upon the falsity already present in him .

**¶10:** And so it is with the divine good dwelling within all things of the natural world, whether scattered throughout the natural mind or extended upon the suffering of the redem pt ive order . When you advance through the natural world along the path of your spiritual life, and in so doing you necessarily press upon the divine good that is dispers ed within natural things, that good takes no reckoning against you in cond emnation or w rath. For it perce ives that you walk upon it for the sake of liberation and spiritual restoration — to proclaim its hidden reality on its behalf. You journey through the natural world because of the divine life within it , to reveal its interior tru ths. And the suffering end ured by the in most structural truths of your being — which you have b urdened through your natural existence — does not tend toward cond emnation, but is ordered toward redem ption.

**¶14:** It is like this: as genuine wisdom undert akes to reverse the course of spiritual disease — when a deep -seated evil is lod ged within the external man — wisdom cuts into the di sordered life with the sharp edge of truth. In its understanding of what must be done, it opens the evil and l ays it bare. Then it applies penet rating truths that have the power to dissolve the falsity bound up with that evil, so that what is hard ened may be loos ened. It may cut with the power of natural truth in its strength , and so cast the evil out, together with the dissol ving tru ths that have done their work. And the deep -seated evil is purified from the burning of self-love that had infl amed it. After this , gentle goods and consol ing truths are laid upon the place where the evil had been — and the mind is made whole. The person who has been regenerated through this process does not generate resent ment in the will against the wisdom that has done this; because he perceives that every operation was directed toward his restoration and spiritual whol eness. After the sharp separation that truth has performed , and the burning application by which evil was laid bare, he even gives the fruits of grat itude to the divine wisdom that he aled him. He renders acknowledg ment from the heart, and remains in conjunction with that wisdom through love for the whole of his life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Again, do not be afraid even with this; because the Living Soul is like this. As a person, if a disease will take hold of his limbs, and his heart [is sl]ow, his soul distressed, and he has pain in his disease. He seeks after a doctor to cure him, to make him strong of heart. And he cures, attends to, and gives him health [from] the disease that has risen up against him. So he thinks about this.

[And] a wise person comes, knowing the formulas proper to a skilled doctor. If he shall achieve a healing of the one whom he [shall vis]it, he recites over him the formulas that he knows, and he even tramples with his foot upon all his limbs! That person, who is ill, knows that this person is trampling upon him so that he might achieve a healing; rather, not doing this to him out of some enmity he had against him beforehand. Instead, all that he does, he does to him that he might make a healing of his body. And he expels [the] disease and the pain, trampling upon him to occasion this benefit. That person, who is ill, he can bear no anger nor hatred against this doctor, who tramples upon him. He can not hate him out of enmity, because he knows that he does this to him to his benefit.

However, should someone come and trample upon him in enmity; he may hate, prevent and not permit him! For he knows that he tramples upon him in enmity; and as he strikes out of a wanton whim, he piles another illness upon his disease.

Again, this too is the case with the Living Soul; whether in the earth, or in the Cross of Light. Should you walk along upon it on the path, should you trample the Cross, it may take no reckoning against you in anger nor wrath. For it knows that [you] walk upon it for relief and healing, to proclaim on its behalf. [You] walk because of it, to reveal its mysteries. Also, the distress of the bones, which you have oppressed, befits not sin, but is set towards the victory. Again, because of this nothing will be lost for you due to the distress of the bones and your toil; rather, it all accumulates to the relief (of the soul).

[He is li]ke this, a wise doctor who might turn back [the course of] his disease. As a wound is in his body, he cuts [into] this person who is ill, in his wisdom, [and] he [lays bare] this wound, and he cuts it. After these things [he cleanses it,] and he places the soluble drugs upon it, so that [they will be able to diss]olve. He might incise it with the iron, and he casts it out [f]rom him, with the soluble drugs. And the wound is purified [fr]om the fever. After these events, he shall place the soothing drugs [upon the wound,] and it heals up. That person, who is ill, he shall give [patience unto the doctor;] but he shall not [bear hatred, and] he [shall not] generate anger in his heart against him; because he knows that he is making the aspect of his benefit and his healing. After the cut that he may make, and the cauterizing that he may do there, he shall even give rewards to the doctor! He gives his thanks and is a friend to him his whole life through.

Rather, the word that wounds is this: should a person utter a saying for the sake of the murder of a person, or the murder of animals, or for [the sake of] the murder of trees and the Cross of Light, the lying word and the wrathful and the bitter, or a word of envy and [malice] only, or a word of accusation, which someone will spread against his brother; this is the [wor]d that wounds [the Living Soul]. Should the person utter it, it befits [si]n; because [he has br]ought forth from it the demons [of darkness. I have spoken] concerning this [to] the righteous person, or [concerning] all of them, which I have proclaimed, in order that [he might not bind] his word to the fetter; because anyone who would [bind] his word to the fetter. And again, he [too, at] his coming forth, they will bind him in the place wherein he has bound his [brother].
